what: Potential adverse operating conditions; neither remaining life nor failure date demonstrated.
lead: Not reported.
signals: Twenty proposed inputs plus component limits.
thresholds: Source thresholds appear in Section 6 and must retain ambiguity flags.
approach: Start with reviewed rated-limit checks; quarantine contradictory thresholds; collect adjudicated failures before training the ANN.
validation_limits: Conceptual study; incomplete feature equations; several threshold/unit/comparator errors; model-specific inputs and extensive downhole/design data required.
project_use: Useful feature/rule inventory; weak predictive evidence.

what: Response to control changes and constraint crossing; not validated remaining life.
lead: Motor response 2–3 hours and intake response 5–10 days; no failure horizon.
signals: State, history, CIPs, production, pump model and metadata.
thresholds: Field-specific values and unit discrepancy in Section 6.
approach: First implement data-quality and stability gates, then shadow-test recommendations with uncertainty and human approval; use tests to verify incremental oil.
validation_limits: Stable wells only; blending confidence algorithm undisclosed; network interference and equivalent injection unresolved; geologist approves settings; sample-count/pressure-unit discrepancies.
project_use: Strong practical optimization architecture for Avalon plus tests; downhole sensor loss limits direct adoption.

what: Possible developing distress/risk, not specific failure or RUL.
lead: 7/30/60 days are analysis windows, not proven warning lead times.
signals: Eight signals plus event masks and confirmed outcomes.
thresholds: Figure 3 prints D=(-100,-0.6,-0.2), C=(-0.5, 0, 0.5), I=(0.2, 0.6,100). Curve shoulders and text's triangle notation need careful implementation; no validated alert DOF threshold.
approach: Implement as explainable hypothesis scores, with unit-consistent slopes, event segmentation and missing-signal coverage; validate specificity before operational use.
validation_limits: Nine selected wells; actual causes not established; scale/unit-sensitive arctangent; common memberships; trip contamination; three identical rule vectors; 30/60-day gaps.
project_use: Highly relevant offshore cautionary case and transparent rules; score reflects architecture/lessons, not proven predictive performance.

what: Abnormal operation potentially preceding failure; not a verified failure mode or exact date.
lead: 12 days in one historical case; hours-to-days threshold tradeoff.
signals: Seven synchronized inputs, variant and historical events.
thresholds: Source examples >80% and <40%; not proven probabilities or field alarm settings.
approach: Train on adjudicated healthy regimes, hold out complete wells/runs, score in shadow mode, calibrate false alerts and provide evidence to engineers.
validation_limits: Architecture/training details undisclosed; causality unclear; manual baseline cleansing; unknown anomalies hard to interpret; repeated historical tuning risks optimism.
project_use: Useful anomaly-monitoring architecture; limited reproducibility and no validated sensor-loss pathway.

what: Developing multivariate instability preceding some trips.
lead: Hours; one illustrated ~30-hour interval.
signals: Historian variables, event log and clean healthy baseline.
thresholds: 95% F-distribution boundary; figure example T² boundary near 10, not transferable.
approach: Build regime-specific robust PCA with run-state masks, contributor display, persistence and false-alert evaluation; keep recommendation assessment outside raw contribution ranking.
validation_limits: Linear normal model; correlated data; anonymized inputs; fixed-other-variable bands are not causal control policy; no held-out performance counts.
project_use: Strong explainable first-stage anomaly framework; reduced-sensor variant requires new validation.

what: Possible failure-associated anomalies.
lead: 12 days in one example, not guaranteed.
signals: Undisclosed process KPIs.
thresholds: None reported.
approach: Use as a concept entry and trace implementation evidence to technical papers, without treating it as an independent validation.
validation_limits: Two-page guest editorial; no reproducible model specification or independent results; probable same Siemens case as P04/P36.
project_use: Useful stakeholder explanation; little implementable engineering detail.

what: Rod-system failure states and pre-signals, not validated ESP failures.
lead: 2/8-month examples reference recorded dates, not verified physical onset.
signals: Rod load/card/production/runtime and adjudicated event labels.
thresholds: Learned model votes; no transferable engineering limits.
approach: Transfer evaluation/label discipline only; establish ESP-specific features, whole-run temporal holdout and alert-event matching.
validation_limits: Rod systems; recorded-date bias; missing-data fill; table inconsistencies; claimed proof of no overfitting contradicted by reported overfit above 180 iterations; record-level CV may leak within wells.
project_use: Methodological comparison; low direct ESP relevance.

what: Abnormal behavior requiring review.
lead: Not quantified here.
signals: Quality synchronized process history; full list not disclosed.
thresholds: Not reported.
approach: Build read-only evidence-backed fleet triage in Copilot, keep existing control/protection workflow and measure alert usefulness.
validation_limits: Architecture-level treatment; root causes and model mechanics undisclosed; availability of unknown downhole inputs not resolved.
project_use: Directly relevant Copilot operating model and user workflow.

what: Current operating-condition diagnosis; no demonstrated failure-date or RUL prediction.
lead: Not reported.
signals: Current, voltage, real-time gas/liquid rates, GLR, surface pressure.
thresholds: Normal current ±5%; illustrative normalized 0.8/1.2; site calibration required; correlation threshold undisclosed.
approach: Implement as ranked hypotheses with test age/coverage visible; collect event-rate electrical data and confirm with fresh tests before causal advice.
validation_limits: Several table/text contradictions; diagrams schematic; current waveform sampling requirement unspecified; live gas/liquid meter unlike intermittent tests; pressure formulas dimensionally ambiguous.
project_use: High relevance to lost downhole sensors, conditional on surface-rate data quality.

what: Anomalous/inefficient state associated with future reported events.
lead: 90 days is evaluation tolerance, not demonstrated per-event warning time.
signals: Electrical, runtime, quality and confirmed events.
thresholds: Site maximum current for cleaning; no universal failure thresholds; SVM boundary learned.
approach: Strong surface-only baseline candidate; retain missingness, mask planned cycling, evaluate chronological run-held-out event precision/recall and false alerts per well-month.
validation_limits: Labels subjective; inefficiency versus failure confused; 90-day window can inflate usefulness; no fixed RUL; copying prior data can manufacture patterns.
project_use: One of the most directly usable electrical-only starting points, with modest reported performance.

what: Service-life estimate conditional on recorded attributes.
lead: No early-warning horizon; post-pull predictor compromises prospective use.
signals: Static metadata, operation cycles, production and valid pre-event solids metric.
thresholds: No ESP alarm thresholds. Beam geometry recommendations must remain separate.
approach: Assemble run-level dataset including censored survivors; replace HUD leakage; validate survival/life models on later installations.
validation_limits: Post-pull HUD risks target leakage; censoring treatment and held-out validation unclear; correlated feature weights are not causes; only failure cases may bias life model.
project_use: Strong reliability-data and leakage lessons; preliminary life model.

what: Candidate RUL, horizon risk and failure class; cause attribution framework separate from prediction.
lead: 30-day risk labels preferred in source; 1/7-day precision weak. Case 12-day and 30–90-day claims are not robust prospective guarantees.
signals: Full as-of feature set, run boundaries, event labels, censoring and sensor-coverage flags.
thresholds: 30/14/7/1-day label horizons; z/IQR data screens; hours-online ≤24 and study choke cap 128/64 inch are data checks, not universal operating alarms.
approach: Rebuild raw-to-feature pipeline with no backward future fill, per-run temporal holdouts/purge, censored survivors and external field tests; compare 30-day RF against simple electrical baseline before RUL.
validation_limits: Conflicting cohort/metric tables, ambiguous split nomenclature, backward filling and full-well imputation risk lookahead, supervised failure clustering may require unavailable future mode, censoring handling unclear, post-event labels mixed with causal categories and WO. Claimed R² '4.0' is invalid as a conventional positive upper-bound score and likely missing a sign; retain as source error.
project_use: Rich ontology/feature catalog and leakage lessons; headline model/economic claims require substantial audit.

what: Rod failure/suboptimal states; ESP extension proposed.
lead: 31-day life-estimation error in abstract is not warning time; no validated ESP lead.
signals: Rod-specific six core signals and event labels.
thresholds: Model scores .5/.75; eligibility 4 h/50 d, not ESP alarm limits.
approach: Transfer data eligibility, whole-well/time holdouts and event-level alert accounting to an ESP pilot.
validation_limits: Rod-specific features; imbalance (~1% failure time) inflates accuracy; retrospective labels use later evidence; cannot use those future observations live; small suboptimal-event cohorts.
project_use: Useful deployment/evaluation workflow; no direct ESP model validation.

what: No validated forecast; improved labels enable future models.
lead: Not reported.
signals: Failure and DIFA evidence plus matched operating history.
thresholds: No validated sensor alarm thresholds; generic thermal-aging statements are not ESP-specific trip settings.
approach: Adopt separate symptom/mode/component/cause/evidence-status fields; retain unknowns and non-failure pulls; later train only on adjudicated histories.
validation_limits: Incomplete RCA, selection/subjective reporting, weak association, counts and category counts not perfectly consistent; counterfactual economics and unsupported discussion percentages.
project_use: High-value Copilot ontology and reliability database foundation; no proven predictive engine.

what: Simulated response and synthetic fault signatures; future RUL/diagnostic capability.
lead: Not reported.
signals: System metadata, telemetry and calibration references.
thresholds: No operational alarm limits; two-minute simulation target is computational cadence.
approach: Begin with calibrated hydraulic/electrical residuals and independent tests; add thermal model and missing-sensor estimates with uncertainty before full twin.
validation_limits: Calibration/identifiability, uncertain physics, sim-to-real gap; stochastic life assignment is not observed RUL; no deployed validation.
project_use: Strong future architecture; too data-intensive for first Copilot release.

what: Aggregate failure risk and pump-component risk.
lead: Nominal 30/45 day labels; historical blind averages about 60 days are a different measurement, with broad ranges including 0 days for well failures.
signals: Measured telemetry, physical model outputs, maintenance/install outcomes.
thresholds: No operational risk cutoff disclosed. >75% data quality over 120 days is a training gate.
approach: Reconstruct independent ESP-run timelines, causal features and physical models; prospective shadow alerts; measure event precision/recall, false alarms per well-month and lead distributions.
validation_limits: Small component sample, SME-corrected event dates, balanced initial test prevalence and retrospective review. Roughly 40% well failures missed. Complete 18-feature names not disclosed.
project_use: Strong hybrid-model design and useful evaluation evidence, with significant sensor and model prerequisites.

what: Aggregate failure risk, strongest near-term horizon.
lead: 1–3 days supported more strongly than 7–14 days. This is forecast-label horizon, not demonstrated maintenance lead for every event.
signals: Daily telemetry, production context, resistance, physics and exposure features.
thresholds: Probability .5 in balanced classification; not a fleet-calibrated operating alarm.85% separation is a modeling assumption.
approach: Use strictly past-only filling; show missingness; split by run/well/time; recalibrate for rare actual failures and compare measured-only versus inferred-feature models.
validation_limits: Balanced 50/50 class evaluation; interpolated/imputed values are not recovered measurements. Akima≤5 day gaps and long-gap moving-average/linear fills may use future data unless made causal. Component/manufacturer/stage metadata unavailable.
project_use: Good evidence for engineered features and horizon-dependent performance; not a ready-to-deploy sensorless model.

what: Departure from normal multivariate operation.
lead: Case-specific hours; no population warning distribution or RUL.
signals: Consistent synchronized multichannel telemetry.
thresholds: 95% confidence bound on T-squared; model-specific, not physical trip.
approach: Fit healthy regime-specific baselines; exclude startup/shutdown transients as appropriate; require persistence and contribution review; evaluate false alerts and event detection.
validation_limits: Limited illustrated cases; no validated causal diagnosis; 95% pointwise bound does not equal 5% fleet event false-alarm rate; operating regime shifts matter.
project_use: Useful early unsupervised pilot; overlaps P05 and must not be counted as independent replication.

what: Abnormal operating conditions; paper demonstrates detection/prescriptive support, not calibrated RUL.
lead: Not established.15/30 min and 24/48 h thresholds are observation windows.
signals: Core 8 channels plus optional vibration/discharge temperature/rating/curves.
thresholds: PIP change: absolute daily-average PIP change >=5% in 24 h; Rapid motor temperature rise: motor temperature increases >=10% over 30 min; Wellhead pressure change: absolute daily-average WHP change >5% in 24 h; Unstable intake/current: PIP standard deviation changes >20% over 24 h; Rapid discharge change: absolute PDP change >=20% over 15 min; Discharge thermal rise: absolute daily-average discharge temperature change >=7% over 48 h; Vibration increase: vibration >20% above installation baseline; High motor loading: motor amps >=90% nameplate at 60 Hz; Loading change: motor loading changes >25% over time; Specific-energy deterioration: source specific-energy/lift metric differs >15% from as-installed; Worn versus plugged head curve: head curve lower over operating range
approach: Implement source-qualified candidate rules with data/frequency gates; retain multiple causes; score evidence completeness; display approved checks and verified operational limits.
validation_limits: Membership thresholds not fully reproducible; overlapping pump patterns; experimental percentages not universal limits; no sensitivity/specificity.
project_use: Highest-value rule/action source for the requested Copilot, provided ambiguity and measurement dependence are retained.

what: Rod pump/tubing failure patterns.
lead: One-month examples; evaluation counts alarms within 60 days.14 day/7 day windows are features, not lead.
signals: Dynamometer/load/runtime and outcome records.
thresholds: ADTree negative score; no transferable physical cutoff.
approach: For ESP build fresh features; avoid interpreting random-peek test adaptation as untouched prospective validation.
validation_limits: Very small event count; random-peek uses unlabeled test distribution (transductive evaluation); high false alarms; inconsistent counts/metrics; smoothing may erase real events.
project_use: Methodological reference; weak direct ESP applicability.

what: Trend-bearing rod pump/tubing failures; abrupt rod/joint events not reliably forecast.
lead: 100 day evaluation tolerance is not proven 100 day advance warning; actual failure may precede recorded discovery.
signals: Load-card/runtime series and independent event dates.
thresholds: 100 nonmissing signatures; normal cluster>50% algorithm versus 70% prose; tubing-card shrinkage lambda unspecified.
approach: Use source methodology to design cross-well ESP study; audit true onset vs discovery date and report abrupt-event detection separately.
validation_limits: 100 day matching tolerance; alerts within 15 days of downtime filtered; different fields vary markedly; prose incorrectly labels false positive as false negative; normal-cluster cutoff 70% prose versus 50% algorithm.
project_use: Useful global-model and evaluation lessons; not an ESP diagnostic source.

what: Off-envelope operation and impending trip risk; no RUL prediction.
lead: Not quantified.
signals: Telemetry plus curves/nameplates/fluid data.
thresholds: Local curve limits and nameplates; 60→80% loading is an example, not alarm threshold.
approach: Start with electrical/rating dashboard, add pressure-based duty for instrumented wells, display uncertainty for sensor-lost wells.
validation_limits: Rate/head inference requires density and calibration; claimed benefits lack control cohort.
project_use: Strong blueprint for practical surveillance and sensor-availability tiers.

what: Present mechanical/sensor fault class; future failure not validated.
lead: Not reported.
signals: Raw accelerometers and speed.
thresholds: No physical alarm cutoffs; spectral roll off.85 is feature definition.
approach: Confirm waveform availability; first run simple spectral/baseline classifiers; split by physical unit/test run before investing in deep fusion.
validation_limits: Labwater data; random record split may share machine/test run signatures; no held-out field run validation or predictive lead; high training cost.
project_use: Useful mechanical fault ontology; low immediate fit without waveform sensors.

what: Electrical preworkover state.
lead: ≤7 day label; point recall 60% does not equal 60% event recall or guaranteed 7 day warning.
signals: Eight synchronized signals, causal moving differences, independent failure/workover records.
thresholds: 1.5 IQR is cleaning threshold, not fault limit; no physical operating cutoff.
approach: Preserve genuine extremes; fit transforms on training only; chronological ESP-run holdout; report event recall, alarm duration, lead and false alerts.
validation_limits: 70/30 versus 70/15/15 split descriptions; random folds not well/run chronological validation; full-data PCA/scaling language risks leakage; tables contain impossible descriptive ordering(mean/std versus max); standardization text says variance rather than SD.
project_use: Good reproducible baseline candidate and polymer mechanism, with validation caveats.

what: Gas mass flow soft sensor, not future failure.
lead: None established.
signals: Total flow and developed head preferred; optional raw vibration/torque.
thresholds: Source introduction says gas-oil ratio should not exceed 10%; definition/dimensions ambiguous and pump-specific—do not use as universal gas fraction trip.
approach: Calibrate against multiphase measurements and physical head calculation across local speed/fluid domain; reject extrapolation and negative unphysical outputs.
validation_limits: Narrow test domain; no offshore validation, failure outcomes or RUL; head/elevation is not simply well depth. Some estimates negative at zero gas.
project_use: Useful virtual-sensor research direction, limited immediate use with sparse tests/lost sensors.

what: Pressure trajectory hypothesis, not established failure/RUL.
lead: Not reported.
signals: Pressure, current, speed, temperature, vibration histories.
thresholds: 30–70 Hz stated as typical range, 52 Hz case; neither is universal operating limit. No validated alarm threshold.
approach: Use only as low-priority concept; define physical target and causal validation before LSTM development.
validation_limits: Assumes build-up failure mechanism; instantaneous failures acknowledged; no non-Newtonian rheology validation or quantified predictive evidence; table lacks units.
project_use: Limited practical evidence; useful primarily as an example of prediction claims needing stronger validation.

what: Some developing faults; abrupt failures may only be detected.
lead: Unquantified; 20 events before recorded failure.
signals: 13 synchronized channels with mode/quality metadata.
thresholds: Maximum training distance, not physical safety limit.
approach: Use high-frequency Avalon data and regime-specific baselines; compare PCA residual/SPE and T² with sphere; test independent runs and record false alerts per operating hour.
validation_limits: Normal/failure sampling resolution differs; only 70% variance retained; 20 min samples miss fast dynamics; same wells contribute healthy/failure periods; small selected normal set.
project_use: Useful realistic evidence on anomaly-monitor limits and missed failures.

what: Deteriorating multivariate behavior, especially electrical cases; no validated RUL.
lead: Well A drift April 2018, failure June 2018(~2 months), source says 3 months; Well B failure-region May 2016 precedes March 2017 sensor issue 10 months and August 2017 terminal failure; not transferable forecast horizon.
signals: Frequency-specific telemetry and quality/electrical integrity records.
thresholds: Tree.5; source typical undervoltage 20% off nameplate requires actual OEM/site settings. No universal PCA radius.
approach: Keep sensor loss separate from physical fault; retain mode-specific baseline; independently test surface-only model and alert-to-confirmed-fault timing.
validation_limits: Small cases; automatic real-time deployment future work; tree labels/sample independence unspecified; months-long retrospective drift can reflect onset/discovery ambiguity.
project_use: Highly relevant to lost-downhole-sensor scenario, with strong caution against treating missing data as healthy.

what: Recurring risk/exposure and duty mismatch, not individual failure time.
lead: Not quantified.
signals: Telemetry plus design and forensic records.
thresholds: No universal numerical warning. Biweekly data review and quarterly optimization are source practices.
approach: Create ESP-run/DIFA taxonomy linking initiating cause, mechanism, failed part and corrective action; verify effectiveness on subsequent runs.
validation_limits: Small field, concurrent interventions, ambiguous improvement percentages/economic units.
project_use: Foundational reliability knowledge for the Copilot and future outcome labels.

what: Stress-pattern detection before possible damage; existing fault diagnosis.
lead: 10/57 events≥1 h before engineer report; stress-to-failure time not calibrated.
signals: Eight core inputs with quality/reference context.
thresholds: ~75% event probability; trend threshold examples~40% strong change,~5% wear; sensor-resolution-specific noise limits.
approach: Implement explainable candidate logic first; calibrate priors locally, abstain on missing critical evidence; measure alarm workload and confirmed outcomes.
validation_limits: Reference tuning after frequency change;~5% unusual wells require tuning; incomplete sensors+unusual conditions degrade accuracy; 57 event selection does not prove universal 100% recall.
project_use: Excellent probabilistic-copilot architecture, with explicit limits important for sensor-lost wells.

what: Present operational class and integrity/performance fault; no validated RUL.
lead: No quantified advance warning; 24 h card is lookback.
signals: Current plus engineered WHP response and physical model.
thresholds: Pressure ratio 0.78/1.5, current ratio 1; learning rate.4 is model setting, not field alarm.
approach: Use production-current mismatch as screening; retain multiple causes; implement pressure interpretation only for approved acquired tests with uncertainty.
validation_limits: Synthetic training and validation not fully characterized; current classes overlap; Figure 5 rendering partly corrupted; empirical 0.78/1.5/1 cutoffs not universal.
project_use: Highly useful sensor-loss diagnostic concept, with additional test/model requirements.

what: Persistent abnormal operation or earlier recognition of existing failure.
lead: Abstract~2 weeks; detailed means 5/40 days. Source explicitly says one event already catastrophic for 14 days before confirmation—do not label all lead as prevention time.
signals: Synchronized minute telemetry, actual vibration for residual method, independent onset/confirmation dates.
thresholds: PCA nominal tail.0027; residual.01;>12/>195 minutes daily and 2 days persistence. These statistical assumptions are not valid fleet guarantees under autocorrelation.
approach: Tune causal alarm persistence by fault urgency; preserve fast protective systems; count missing minutes separately; validate on healthy and failed runs.
validation_limits: Six failed wells only; parameter selection retrospective; no fleet rate denominator; two-day persistence delays fast faults; real-power proxy I×V omits three-phase power factor/efficiency.
project_use: Useful alarm aggregation and data-quality lessons; reported warning needs onset audit.

what: Current fault diagnosis/ranking; early recognition of some progressing conditions.
lead: Not established as a transferable forecast horizon.30–60 min general assertion is not evidence for all ESP failure modes.
signals: Surface electrical/pressure/temperature plus reliable rate estimates and metadata.
thresholds: Normalized>1 termed overload, cap 1.5; normal-reference exceedance is not equipment-rated overload. Partial associations/exclusions retained for audit, not approved rules.
approach: Start with curated symptoms and soft candidate ranking, not full architecture; keep alternatives, unknown state and evidence provenance; validate independent wells and calibrated confidence.
validation_limits: Restricted private data/graph; hard exclusions physically overbroad; random event split not external-field validation; equation 8 accuracy omits TN and F1 derivation inconsistent; confidence scores from two models may be incomparable; exact 50-label taxonomy not cleanly enumerated.
project_use: Strong conceptual fit for sensor-lost offshore wells; rules need substantial engineering review.

what: Exploratory lifetime association and final-period failure classification.
lead: Not quantified; source explicitly describes some predictions as failure happening.
signals: Current-defined periods, independent event labels and operating context.
thresholds: Tree cutoffs are fitted retrospective partitions, not control settings.
approach: Use past-only rolling exposure; retain censored runs and competing shutdown reasons; assess survival models with independent future runs.
validation_limits: Completed-run summaries leak future information if used as prospective predictors; only 29/42 failure cases; correlated features; no reliable external validation or forecast lead.
project_use: Useful time segmentation and leakage lesson; thermal SAGD limits offshore transfer.

what: Operational state according to retrospective rules; superiority in future failure prediction not established.
lead: No validated forecast horizon; 2–4 h/1 h conditions and 4 h plots are not demonstrated advance warning.
signals: Eight physical variables plus causal engineered trends and independent outcomes.
thresholds: 90°C,.02 g delta,−100 psi/min are study-specific and internally inconsistent with distribution; not approved ESP limits.
approach: Benchmark direct rules against trees using independent DIFA/trip labels; fit preprocessing within training folds; grouped chronological holdout and event-level alarms; preserve genuine anomalies.
validation_limits: One well, selected anomalous window; labels depend on same signals as features; no independent event-level prospective validation; chronological versus stratified K-fold descriptions conflict; preprocessing/SMOTE placement unclear; outlier removal may discard true faults; claimed 5 PC variance 90/95/97% inconsistent.
project_use: Feature-engineering reference; evidence contradictions limit confidence in quantitative claims.

what: Abnormal behavior preceding some interruptions; not RUL or unique cause.
lead: One 12 day case; no guaranteed horizon.
signals: Seven process variables plus quality/event records.
thresholds: ~80% versus<40% anomaly-score examples; final operating cutoff undisclosed.
approach: Pilot in advisory mode with cohort-specific baseline and prospective event/alert audit; compare simple PCA/tree baselines before deep model.
validation_limits: Manual training-data curation; repeated tuning on same history; missing cause specificity; limited reproducibility; related publications reuse pilot evidence.
project_use: Useful advisory surveillance architecture; limited quantitative evidence.

what: Abnormal behavior preceding some interruptions; not RUL or unique cause.
lead: One 12 day case; no guaranteed horizon.
signals: Seven process variables plus quality/event records.
thresholds: ~80% versus<40% anomaly-score examples; final operating cutoff undisclosed.
approach: Pilot in advisory mode with cohort-specific baseline and prospective event/alert audit; compare simple PCA/tree baselines before deep model.
validation_limits: Manual training-data curation; repeated tuning on same history; missing cause specificity; limited reproducibility; related publications reuse pilot evidence.
project_use: Useful advisory surveillance architecture; limited quantitative evidence.
